parsedVerdict.reasoning: All three files are Express middleware for the request pipeline: checking the API key, validating the request body against a schema, and handling errors. They share one convention: the validators throw objects with {name, message} fields and never write responses themselves. errorHandlerMiddleware is the only place that maps error names to HTTP status codes, so no rule is copied across files and the module's own error path is never bypassed. Weaknesses that don't amount to a failure: the error names are plain strings shared between files with no shared error type, and the handler repeats the same log-and-send block within one file. Likely bugs outside this rule: the handler has no return after each case, so it can send twice; the async throw in apiKeyValidator isn't caught by plain Express 4; and apiKey.toString() crashes if the header is missing.
